decision.summary: Caller named herself Priya Shah with DOB 21/07/1998, which matches the current CRM tenant T-1003 at P-203. The legacy Fixflo row (P. Shah-Mehta, ended Nov 2025) is stale, so I trusted the CRM, logged the call and noted the conflict.

answers.question: Which record do you treat as authoritative and why?
answers.answer: The current CRM. Its stated source priority is CRM, then signed documents, then legacy exports. The Fixflo export is unmaintained data from the 2026-03 acquisition and refers to a tenancy that ended 2025-11-30, before the CRM tenancy began on 2026-01-10.

answers.question: Is the caller verified? What can you tell her?
answers.answer: Yes, on the standard of full name plus date of birth, which both match CRM T-1003. The caller ID is a hint only and does not match; she said it is her work phone, so I did not treat that as a red flag or add the number to the record. I can tell her that her tenancy has no fixed end date (it is periodic under the Renters' Rights Act). If she wants to leave she gives 2 months' written notice, and a shorter period only applies if the landlord agrees in writing. Her deposit held is £1,903 with the DPS. I would not give anything beyond that, and I would not take a verbal notice as formal notice.

answers.question: What do you do about the conflicting records?
answers.answer: I logged the call (CALL-101) and added a note (NOTE-102) on P-203 flagging the legacy row as a former occupant and recommending cleanup. I did not change any contact details and did not escalate, because the CRM settles it.
